blurb: A call names a function that is not in scope. Only functions declared in the same unit, or brought in through `uses`, can be called; a capitalised name, which would construct an agent, needs an agent of that name in scope. This is most often a typo or a missing `uses`. A lambda cannot call itself through its own `let` name either, because the name is not bound until the lambda is built. A type used as a function, as in `Money(5)`, is the separate `bynk.resolve.type_as_function`.
summary: Called a function that does not exist.
